subject: TTFT & streaming emit patterns — pilot scope and next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@quantapay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: TTFT & streaming emit patterns — pilot scope and next steps

Thanks for the demo earlier, Alex — good visibility into the payments reconciliation use case. Wanted to capture the performance items we discussed and confirm next steps for a short pilot focused on serving latency and streaming behaviour. Summary and asks below.

Quick recap of QuantaPay goals (from your call):
- Primary: keep end-user first-response feeling instantaneous on web checkout flows (target perceived latency <= 200 ms).
- Measurable TTFT target: aiming for 120–180 ms P50 on standard 256-token prompts for the reconciliation summarizer.
- Throughput: steady-state 200 TPS across three regional nodes, with traffic bursts up to 800 TPS for 60–90s during batch settlements.
- Streaming: prefer SSE for browser clients, but want compatibility with WebSocket for mobile. Chunk cadence: prefer small incremental emits (approx 50–100 ms inter-chunk) to populate UI progressively rather than one big final payload.

Open questions we promised to confirm:
1) Can Redwood guarantee TTFT P50 in the 120–180 ms window in our hosted environment with the quantized model profile we discussed?
2) What fallback behaviour do you recommend when burst concurrency pushes us past dedicated capacity (graceful degrade to a smaller model vs queued requests)?
3) For SSE chunk cadence, is there built-in jitter control to avoid synchronization-related spike patterns?

Next steps proposed:
- Redwood provides a 2-week pilot plan and profiling run to validate TTFT and chunk cadence with a synthetic trace matching your burst profile (we'll share sample traces).
- QuantaPay provides a canonical prompt set + one synthetic traffic trace and grants us a read-only dataset of 500 representative chats for sampling.
- Align on acceptance criteria (P50 TTFT, P95 tail, and visible chunk start latency for SSE).

Attaching a short prototype demo plan and an initial profiler run we ran against a local quantized build (see attachments). Ben/Evelyn — can you add anything technical I missed?

Thanks,
Sergio
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming emit patterns — pilot scope and next steps

Thanks, Sergio — quick technical clarifications from our side after reviewing the prototype artifacts. High level answers to your open questions:

1) TTFT feasibility: with the model variant we discussed (7B quantized to int4, optimized kernels) we are typically seeing P50 TTFT between 80–150 ms on our hosted GPU pools for 256-token prompts, assuming warm KV caches and continuous batching. The 120–180 ms target is achievable but depends on sample-level sequence length variance and cold-cache scenarios. We'll instrument warm/cold markers in the pilot.

2) Fallback strategy: recommended pattern is multi-tier routing —
  - Tier A (preferred): route to dedicated pool pinned to QuantaPay for low-latency traffic.
  - Tier B (fallback): route to a smaller/cheaper variant with lower token accuracy but sub-250 ms TTFT for degraded mode.
  - Tier C (last resort): queue with fast rejection + client-side retry hints.
We can configure automatic model fallback on overload and surface count metrics to your UI.

3) SSE chunk cadence: our runtime supports emit pacing and jitter windows. Default cadence is deterministic (batch emit at 50 ms), but we can add randomized jitter +/- 10–20 ms to avoid synchronized bursts. We'll expose these knobs in the pilot config.

Notes on measuring acceptance: recommend P50/P95 TTFT, first-chunk latency (time to first chunk byte after request), and percent of requests served by Tier A. We'll add tracing hooks so your infra team can correlate frontend render times with server-side TTFT.

Attaching profiler CSV from our internal run (profiler_results_qp_v1.csv) that includes KV cache warm/cold rows — use as a baseline.

—Ben

Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 07:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming emit patterns — pilot scope and next steps

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from QuantaPay side:

- Confirmed that perceived latency target <= 200 ms is product goal; our backend budget for server-side TTFT is 120–140 ms P50 to allow for network + render. We can accept a P95 up to 350 ms during heavy tails.
- Throughput numbers are correct: our e2e test harness can emit the 800 TPS burst profile. We'll provide a CSV trace for the pilot.
- SSE is preferred for the web checkout embed; mobile teams will plan for WebSocket but need identical chunk semantics (first-chunk latency and small inter-chunk spacing).

Constraints and asks:
- Data constraints: we can only share synthetic traces and prompt sets; no production PII. We'll scrub and hand over a 500-record synthetic sample this week.
- Pilot window: we prefer the pilot to run for two business weeks with a 3-day ramp and a 3-day soak at target traffic.

Action items for Redwood:
- Provide a short pilot-runbook and checklist saying what you will measure and how acceptance will be calculated.
- Confirm the exact model variants you will use for Tier A and Tier B and the quantization/latency expectations.

I'll slack you the sample traces by EOB PST today. Can we lock in a kickoff on Wednesday 18th at 10am PT?

—Alex
